text.p: Morocco plans to sell controlling-assets, 34.57 percent stake or 4.1 million state shares in Banque Nationale pour le Developpement, an official at the ministry of privatisation said on Monday.

"The Moroccan state plans to cede its 34.57 percent stake in BNDE...Candidates who want to join the hard core of investors for the purchase of some or all of the shares for sale, should declare their interests," the official told Reuters.
He said the bids should be sent to the Paris-based bank Lazard Freres et compagnie or to Casablanca-based Upline Securities stockbroker.
The closing date for the tender was set for 31 January 1997.
The bank's other shareholders are the private conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement, French Lyonnaise de Banque, Kuwait Investment Company and a group of Moroccan insurance companies.
The bank made a net profit of 18.08 million dirhams in the first half of 1996 and expects around 65 million dirhams as net profit for the all year 1996.
BNDE is among the country's 18 banks which hold an estimated 40 percent of total market capitalisation in 1996, a market analyst said.
BNDE, which is a liquid stock, was last traded at 145 dirhams, he said.
The Casablanca bourse has 47 listed companies including eight banks.
